title: Days Out With Teenagers They’ll Actually Enjoy
description: Days out with teenagers that beat the eye-roll: thrill parks, escape rooms, experience days, city trips and outdoor adventures, and how to save.
h1: Days out with teenagers they’ll actually enjoy
intro: Teens can be the toughest crowd. The trick is giving them some choice and a bit of adrenaline. Here are days out that teenagers genuinely rate.

image.alt: Riders with arms in the air on a roller coaster

cardText: Thrill parks, escape rooms, experiences and how to save on teen tickets.

blocks.title: Scout’s teen tip
blocks.text: Let them pick the day out, and maybe bring a friend. A teen who chose the plan is a teen who enjoys the plan.
points: Check when “child” tickets stop: often at 12 or 15
Students may get discounts with ID
Thrill parks: check height limits for younger siblings

sections.html: Big coasters at Thorpe Park and Alton Towers, or Europa-Park and PortAventura abroad. Arrive at opening and use single rider lines. See our queue tips.

• Escape rooms and immersive games.
  • Indoor climbing, trampoline parks and go-karting.
  • Experience days like junior driving or indoor skydiving.
  • Studio tours, like the Harry Potter Studio Tour.
A day exploring a city (shopping, street food and a show) or a proper outdoor adventure (coasteering, kayaking or a mountain hike with a guide) often goes down better than “a nice walk”.
Many attractions charge adult prices from 12, 15 or 16, so check the age bands. Family tickets, rail 2FOR1 and annual passes help.

faqs.q: What are good days out for teenagers in the UK?
faqs.a: Thrill parks like Thorpe Park and Alton Towers, escape rooms, climbing and go-karting, studio tours, city days and outdoor adventures like coasteering.
